title: Religion
description: The words of the religion — and its own page.
html:
THE RELIGION

Religion

IdeGloss
afan. divination; shells used in divination
agbàlàn. woman of great influence; fertility deity; A. the author of fertility, one of the manifestations of Olisa, Creator
agwùn. spirit of divination; male name
àjàn. sacrifice (joyless, to drive out evil); sacrifice
akalan. power (from the Buddhist deity Mahakala); deity. Etymology: Buddhist Mahakala.
alun. abomination; hurtful, obnoxious thing; taboo
n. spirit; divinity; deity
anyaūn. sun (as heavenly body)
azin. present generation; young people (of present); the younger generation; curse
dibièn. seer/priest (conducts rituals, interprets divine will).
èbùnu Idemmīlithe ram of the Idemili god (This ram lives mainly in the Idemili god's shrine and its surroundings. But it also roams about the village from compound to compound. The ram must not be eaten or killed by anybody, as it is believed that anyone who does this will automatically be visited and killed by the god.)
ekeroyal Python (Python regius), the smaller species of python, more common, lives in compounds and is freely handled, sacred in most parts of Igboland
enen. people, e.g. “nde nka.” ene is used when referring to dead ancestors.
sacred cow (efi Igbò type) owned by village; cannot be killed; if it dies, it is given burial like a human
feworship; serve
gbanav. seek refuge with a deity
godeity worship; to call upon deity. E.g. go alusi
Ika dibien. high priest (oversees the central temple, while Ika Mmuo is specifically for the cathedral at the royal town, Ide).
ika mmụọn. high priest (oversees the central temple, while Ika Mmuo is specifically for the cathedral at the royal town, Ide).
ikalan. king ("half human, half spirit"). Etymology: From Igbo Okala mmadụ, okala mmụọ.
isiafaisiana head dibie; odiana bishop
isianaodiana diocese
itun. deity of creativity & arts
iwu uchun. baptism
mmuon. spirit.
mọ akalan. deity of power. etymology: buddhist "mahakala".
mzùn. "mastery in craft" (blacksmithing, carving, sacred art)
nchun. sacrifice bowl. Etymology: From nchu aja; used at shrines.
nden. people, e.g. “nde nka.” ene is used when referring to dead ancestors.
ndenkan. guild; The Ide Sacred Artisan Order
ndoseodiana temple
nlutaboo; replaces aruru ana
nru anataboo; replaces aruru ana
nyaun. sun (as heavenly body)
obichukwucathedral; central ndose
odianan. ide religion. Etymology: Odinana (Igbo) + Asian/African fusion.
ofov. truth; symbol of justice, righteousness, and authority, which descends from the ancestors, represented by a small piece of wood
ogban. cave; pyramid devoted to a deity (pyramid like nsude)
okwụ̀shrine
olisen. supreme God
osaidivinity
osen. supreme God
osen. God
osekeefirst holy bath; baptism
osianan. a godly tree planted with an umbilical cord, represented by a tree
sịpersonal god. Replaces chi.
